html:
One Xia: Turning a Fractured Wulin into Haless's Righteous State

Survey region (English rating-table classification): Haless.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Long (87 direct missions, plus the shared Xiaken route) | Mission-tree update: locally implemented; exact rework date unconfirmed | Uniqueness: High | Tedium: Medium-high | Early pressure: High | Expansion: High.

One Xia is a linked Xiaken campaign chain: it does not split every Xiaken, Wulin, or pre-formation minor into a separate entry, but records the shared middle and late campaign of Y99 One Xia. The currently confirmed standard historical entrances are Y28 Jiangliusi, Y31 Rang Nartak, Y35 Liukhexingzhe, and Y39 P'ezarang: the first uses Wulin, while the other three use Xiaken. Y58 Lot Dekkhang is a monarchy using Teplinbasiyeti and High Philosophy; Y89 Yuanszi is an oligarchic republic following the Devouring Path. Neither is a standard Y99 predecessor. Y89 may be treated only as a non-standard detour with its own storyline, not as a normal Xiaken entrance. You begin from a Halessi entrance, first unify the Xianjie under pressure from the Command, and then use Y99's theocratic reform, qi cultivation, martial arts, and righteous missions to expand local schools into a state spanning Haless.【Local scripts】【Local localisation】

Identity and history

The base Mod defines Y99 as One Xia, while the current Chinese localisation displays 一侠. The history file is a post-formation country definition: it uses a theocratic government, the Wulin reform, the Righteous Path, the Halessi technology group, and capital 4559. Y99 is therefore not an independent starting country in the same sense as its listed predecessors. The Xiaken connected to it is not another country that must be entered as a separate article. Shared missions use the potential condition has_government_attribute = is_in_xia; Xiaken and independent Xiaken reforms represent the subject and independent-martial-artist institutions within the Wulin political system.【Local history scripts】【Local scripts】

Country story and campaign line

The formal scope is one continuous Xiaken-country chain. Its predecessors can differ in culture, school, and military position, but the formation decision ultimately changes the country to Y99, removes Wulin where applicable, adds the one_xia reform, and replaces non-generic missions. The war formation route requires ownership of 4559, at least 30 provinces carrying the rightful_xia_territory modifier, Y99 not already existing, and the relevant Xiaken/formation conditions. The peaceful route requires the relevant Xiaken and independent Xiaken countries to no longer exist before the same Y99 change and mission replacement. This is why Y99 is the unification result, not a collective alias for every Xiaken country.【Local scripts】

Y99 has 87 direct missions. The direct groups are the qi, heroes, legends, consolidation, One Xia, foreign, liberation, road, and temple lines recorded in the current mission files. The opening develops qi, chooses a martial school, and handles Jianxu Temple. The middle takes the righteous path from local disputes into fighting monsters, cleansing demonic monasteries, and sending envoys to surrounding lands. The later line connects righteous liberation, roads across Haless, and a temple network to a wider continental project. Its central tension is not merely that the state uses war: One Xia claims to oppose tyranny, oppression, and class hierarchy, while the actual tools available to it remain theocracy, subject integration, forced incorporation choices, and continued expansion. The claim and the institution must remain separate.【Local scripts】【Official development diary】

Core mechanics

First, Wulin and Xiaken provide a layered reform structure. The xiaken reform supplies military structures involving generals, heirs, morale, infantry, and martial units, while binding the country to Xianjie politics. The independent-Xiaken reform retains a similar military-political framework without dependence on a Wulin overlord.

Second, the formation decision is a unification system rather than a simple rename. The war route must handle Xiaken subjects and the territorial threshold before changing the country to Y99; the peaceful route requires the relevant reform countries to disappear. Formation then removes or replaces the old institutions and missions according to the actual decision path.【Local scripts】

Third, qi and martial-school development form a long cultivation loop. Missions connect military tradition, training, martial schools, national development, and event choices. Some outcomes depend on decisions and events, so static national ideas alone do not describe the full system.

Fourth, religion and roads turn the righteous claim into institutions. The missions spread the righteous paths across broad territory, establish pilgrimage and road infrastructure, and use righteous war goals to turn liberation into concrete diplomatic and military actions. Roads and temples are therefore part of the state-building loop, not merely flavour.

Fifth, succession and theocratic politics keep affecting the campaign after formation. Ruler quality, heirs, sect decisions, temple relationships, and succession arrangements alter the way the country handles its military and its expanding realm. The five systems overlap; none should be compressed into a single generic “martial nation” description.【Local scripts】

Staged play

The predecessor stage is about survival first. The Xianjie is pressed by the Command, Bianfang, and other regional powers; a small entrance should not treat the formation threshold as immediately reachable. Use the military quality supplied by the Xiaken framework, the subject/overlord relationship, and shared missions to push unification, while keeping enough administrative and diplomatic resources to satisfy the formation conditions. The predecessor's identity and position change the opening: the listed standard entrances do not begin from the same strength, reforms, or diplomatic situation.

The middle phase is about the Xianjie core, martial-school choices, qi stages, and heir development. Annexing every minor too early can remove a useful subject structure and alter the route through shared missions; waiting too long allows the Command or a nearby power to consume the targets. The player must therefore balance immediate survival, formation progress, and the institutional setup that will still matter after Y99 exists.

After formation, the 87 missions raise the scale sharply. The country handles northern monsters and demonic threats, sends envoys, spreads the righteous paths, constructs roads and temples, and brings multicultural territory into a unified narrative. Mission claims, subjects, and war goals are strong, but the central position exposes One Xia to the Command, Bianfang, Lakin, and southern powers. The endgame is a long project of religious networks, army quality, and governing capacity, not a one-click “all Haless” button.【Local scripts】

Formable countries and endgame

One Xia is the post-formation Y99 endpoint. Internal name or reform changes are not new country entries. Predecessors shape the opening; Y99 provides the shared middle and late campaign.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion/building 86/100 | Autocracy/liberty 68/100 | Magic↔artifice 63/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 58/100) | Pluralism/uniformity 78/100.

The v2.1 values result is Neutral (63/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory. It suits players who enjoy formation chains, martial development, theocracy, and long Halessi missions; avoid it if you want a small peaceful core or dislike powerful early neighbours. Community experience is route- and version-dependent.【Community views】

Evidence boundary

The base Mod determines formation, mission ownership, and reform relationships. The older local DOCX records “Jiangliusi → One Xia” as a continuous route and is useful as a historical/player-document boundary, but it does not replace the current formation decisions or mission scripts. The exact-title One Xia, Y99, and Xia searches returned no result; the related Xiaken page was read and only supports the limited Xiaken background stated in the evidence receipt. No related-only Wiki result is treated as proof of One Xia-specific history. Full paths, the old-DOCX continuity evidence, formation conditions, and gaps are in the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply on adoption, seven ideas unlock in order, and the ambition applies after all seven. Racial, government, and mission rewards are excluded; formation ideas do not automatically stack with old ideas. Idea descriptions may recount history or describe future ideals; they do not by themselves establish that the described events had occurred by 1444.

One Xia (Y99) — One Xia Ideas

Traditions: One Xia Traditions

Effect: Army morale: +15%; Manpower from true faith provinces: +20%.

Idea 1: Many Schools into One Path

The Xianjie is a diverse realm of martial arts, heroes, and devotion to self perfection. With many of the different temples and techniques combined into a new united nation, the One Xia now commands the fiercest group of fighters Haless has ever seen.

Effect: Infantry combat ability: +15%.

Idea 2: Stewards of the Xiadao

At the center of Halann lies Xiadao, the birthplace of the Accretive Path and the start of the Xia alliance. The highly devoted people of the Xianjie regard it as the most sacred place in the realm, frequently visiting to pay respects and take great care in maintaining the city's image.

Effect: True faith tolerance: +1; Prestige: +1.

Idea 3: Righteous War Against Evil

The One Xia has many enemies that surround its borders, with evil practitioners of dark magic to the north, the terrifying disciplined Command to the west, and the tyrannical warlord of Bianfang to the east.

All of these foes have a united goal of destroying the One Xia, and crushing the heart of the Accretive Path. The masters of the Xia must enlighten these enemies on the power of the true faith, and liberate these regions from evil once and for all.

Effect: Missionary strength: +2%; War score cost against other religions: -15%.

Idea 4: Creation of the Righteous Conclave

Although the One Xia was united in name, many of the temples still had issues with rival monks who they fought against in the past. To resolve these disputes, while also centralizing the government, the Righteous Conclave was established, a parliament filled with all of the masters in the Xianjie created to settle affairs both internally and externally.

This council efficiently solved the petty issues that plagued the nation and expanded the government's power to become a competent centralized state.

Effect: Administrative capacity modifier: +20%.

Idea 5: Master Among Masters

The top master of the One Xia must be the strongest of his peers, and a master is frequently challenged to one-on-one duels for the role. While this seems like an unstable way of leadership to foreigners, this tradition keeps the title of Righteous Master limited to only the most powerful fighters.

Effect: Monarch military skill: +1.

Idea 6: The Fragrant Domain

A common nickname for the Xianjie and its numerous temples, as it produces most of the incense and scented materials that are traded throughout all of Haless. Merchants coming to the Xianjie are able to know that they arrived just based on smell alone, and the incense they buy from the One Xia is used for ceremonies, perfume, and even therapeutic purposes.

Effect: Production efficiency: +10%.

Idea 7: A Classless Society

The Accretive and Transmutative Paths are religions practiced by the common people, with many of the local village legends being incorporated into the faith. The Two Path were made by the commonfolk and practiced faithfully by them, and as a result the One Xia was a state which abandoned the ideas of their neighbors.

Eliminating any concept of the class societies found in the Raj and Yanshen, the people of the One Xia believed that no one is born into a social class, and the worth of a person would be determined by their contributions to their society.

Effect: National unrest: -2.

Ambition: One Xia Ambition

Effect: Army tradition: +0.5.

Jiangliusi (Y28) — Jiangliusi Ideas

Traditions: Jiangliusi Traditions

Effect: Advisor cost: -10%; Trade efficiency: +10%.

Idea 1: School of Flowing Water

The disciples of the School of Flowing Water are taught to be swift in combat, to strike with unstoppable force, and to always be open to change or innovation. Most Flowing Water masters are magically gifted, and the School claims a deep connection with the ancient water spirits of the Youxiahe.

Effect: Army morale: +10%.

Idea 2: The Jiangliubao

At the end of the Youxiahe, an ancient fortress monastery lies atop a river isle. Known as the Jiangliubao, this citadel is the home of the School of Flowing Water, the political and economic center of Xianjie, and the capital of the Xia. The Jiangliubao is purported to be practically un-siegeable, having fallen only twice - once to Harimar, and then to Jaher.

Effect: Fort defense: +20%.

Idea 3: A Land Between Lands

The forests of Xianjie lie between the two lands of Rahen and Yanshen, and Jiangliusi lies at the center of Xianjie. Consequently, the monks of Jiangliusi and their river fortress play host to much of the traffic flowing between the two lands.

Effect: Global institution spread: +25%.

Idea 4: Founders of the Xia

Many centuries ago, the followers of the Accretive and Transmutative Paths ranged far and wide across Haless, bowing to no sovereign and practicing their martial arts in the ways that each individual saw fit. In the early 200s, during the chaos in the wake of Harimar's death, the various schools united under the leadership of one nominal sovereign: Jiangliusi.

Effect: Prestige: +1.

Idea 5: Inviting the Righteous Masters

In 270, First Master Kai Jiàn invited all Righteous Masters of the Xia to meet in a summit at the Jiangliubao. As the empire of Harimar dissipated into ashes and the chaos of civil war subsided, the disparate Xiaken were becoming restless and unruly, so Master Jiàn sought to reinforce the bonds between them so as to keep the young Xia united. After many days of heated debate - both rhetorical and martial - it was decided unanimously that the event would become a tradition. Every decade, the Righteous Masters of the various schools and paths of the Xia meet in the Jiangliubao to discuss the direction of the Xia.

Effect: Subject liberty desire: +1000%.

Idea 6: Masters of Hydropower

The masters of the School of Flowing Water unsurprisingly have a great affinity for water, and even those disciples who are not magically gifted have an intangible connection to the rivers of Xianjie.

The banks surrounding the Jiangliubao are lined with water mills and other, more magical devices of their design, making use of hydropower not only to mill grain but to irrigate fields or forge metal. Some are even rumoured to be hotspots of river nymph activity.

Effect: Goods produced modifier: +10%.

Idea 7: A New Xia

This new age has brought about a myriad of innovations and challenges, each one straining the Xia further and further. If Jiangliusi wishes to keep its position at the head of the Accretive Path, it must solidify its control over the unruly Xiaken.

Effect: Subject tribute income: +25%; Subject force-limit contribution: +100%.

Ambition: Jiangliusi Ambition

Effect: Diplomatic reputation: +100%.

Rang Nartak (Y31) — Rang Nartak Ideas

Traditions: Rang Nartak Traditions

Effect: Cavalry combat ability: +15%; Construction cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Veterans of Harimar

Unlike many of the Xianjie, who can claim to have inhabited this land since time immemorial, we have arrived relatively recently with the invasion of Harimar. We were originally driven out of Ghavaanaj by a coalition of weaker tribes, and were accepted into Harimar's army. After achieving many victories, we were allowed to settle in an empty area of Xianjie, now known as Rang Nartak. We then converted to the Accretive Path, and have assimilated into local culture. Our people still take justifiable pride in that we forged our own home, and our legacy as hardened warriors continues to inspire soldiers in the present.

Effect: Prestige decay: -1%.

Idea 2: School of the Elephant

Though we left our original homeland, we still maintain the tradition of elephant warfare, mixed with unique martial powers.

Our tactics rely on using our elephants in a devastating attack, which is sure to pulverize any enemy. Once the enemy is routed, we hurl lighting-powered javelins into the ranks of the retreating soldiers. With the combination of these two individually powerful techniques, none shall be able to stand against us!

Effect: Cavalry shock: +25%.

Idea 3: Light of Victory

On the fourth day of the month known as Nerament to the men from distant shores, our nation celebrates the holiday of Shèngzhan, the Light of Victory. Everyone wears white to symbolize their purity, and paint roads and temple walls with different designs created by dyes and pigments. This is all done to symbolize the belief that righteousness will always conquer darkness, and dates back to the beginning of our nation.

When we fled the lands of Rahen, we thought all was lost, but we found a new home, prompting our leader to declare a day of remembrance. This is the holiday that we celebrate in the same form today.

Effect: Stability cost modifier: -20%.

Idea 4: Colored Robe System

How are we to know if a recruit is qualified? This is a question that has baffled many nations, but ours has discovered a solution. Each monk of Rang Nartak is granted a white robe at the beginning of training, with the possibility to obtain a new color of robe after defeating 10 opponents in single combat.

Any aspirant must advance through yellow, orange, green, blue, purple, brown, red, and gray before completing their training. After this, they may rejoin the temple as a master to train new students. This system ensures that all aspirants are qualified, and gives students a definitive goal to focus on.

Effect: Army tradition: +0.5.

Idea 5: The Righteous Family

A famous saying in Rang Nartak is that 'when a new master is chosen, their entire family is chosen.' What this means in practical terms is that when a new master takes power over the nation, they bring their family members to court with them, where they typically act as advisors.

While these recruits may be of dubious quality, it does occasionally bring competent people to the forefront without having to go through traditional channels. They are also willing to accept lower compensation, which will certainly help our finances.

Effect: Ruler culture advisor cost: -15%; Possible advisors: +1.

Idea 6: Dredges of Society

To our south lies the sprawling city of Sarisung, filled to the brim with criminals and the downtrodden. We accept all in order to spread the Accretive Path, and as such we permit some of these vagabonds into the military. This both saves the spiritual lives of these men and makes them very loyal to our nation for lifting them out of poverty, giving us an unparalleled pool of manpower for our size. While some of the more odious criminals do cause problems from time to time, this is a worthy price to pay for the salvation of these mens' souls - and their bodies in combat.

Effect: Global manpower modifier: +15%.

Idea 7: Elephant Pageants

Elephants, being the backbone of our war plans and a major component of our culture, are incredibly prestigious to own. Thus, the realm has many pageants where families can show off their finest elephants, and the best amongst them can be nominated. This has led to an increase in breeding, as families breed their best to create finer offspring in a quest for glory.

While these developments have only increased the quality of our herd by a bit, it has increased the quantity of elephants by an vast amount. This lets us field more elephant-mounted warriors, as opposed to regular infantry, which will let us dominate in the wars to come.

Effect: Cavalry cost: -15%.

Ambition: Rang Nartak Ambition

Effect: Leader siege: +1.

Liukhexingzhe (Y35) — Liukhexingzhe Ideas

Traditions: Liukhexingzhe Traditions

Effect: Shock damage received: -10%; Land force-limit maintenance modifier: -10%.

Idea 1: Way of the Drunken Fist

While many armies rely on their discipline or courage to defeat their enemies, we utilize speed. Our enemies cannot react to our swift strikes, letting us cut them down in droves. This speed also allows us to strike in unorthodox places, confusing our opponents and bypassing their defenses.

The reason we are the only nation to use this tactic is because it demands a special beverage that is made only in our temples, enhancing our warriors' endurance and agility and allowing for their extreme speed. While inebriation is a common side effect of consuming this great drink, it is worth the price for such effectiveness.

Effect: Infantry shock: +15%.

Idea 2: The Realm of Celebrations

When one thinks of our monasteries, they think of one of our parties. Whether it is for a great victory or for the inauguration of a new master, we will take any opportunity to stage one of our signature parties. This has led to great happiness among the population, as well as great fame abroad. Even in the lands of the tiger-kings of Rahen, our parties are spoken of in awe.

Effect: Prestige decay: -1%.

Idea 3: Temples of Wine

While many other Xiaken produce such base goods as silk or incense, we produce the most valuable of all earthly goods - alcohol. Each temple competes to produce the finest brew, which is then sold to other states.

Our spirits are not only used for profit; the finest are always saved for our lavish feasts and to support our unique fighting style. While others produce goods that have no practical value, we produce a good that is both useful and joyful.

Effect: Production efficiency: +10%.

Idea 4: Loyalty to the Wulin

Unlike certain other monasteries, our loyalty to the Wulin has been unquestionable. While other monasteries refuse tribute and send him away, we offer extra tribute and invite him to improve our mutual relations. This has improved both our standing with the Wulin and the expertise of our diplomats, letting us make both peace and brew into the foreseeable future.

Effect: Diplomatic reputation: +100%; Diplomats: +1.

Idea 5: The 108 Vagabonds

Once, our future seemed lost, our temples besieged and our armies shattered. The hosts of the Kai had prevailed in every action, confronting us with the specter of annihilation. In our darkest hour, a group of wandering monks, known as the 108 Vagabonds, began their campaign. They harassed supply lines, aided our forces, and sought techniques in the most ancient of ruins. Using all of this and the Drunken Fist Style, the Vagabonds drove off the Kai, enshrining themselves forever in the memory of our nation and its people.

Effect: National unrest: -2.

Idea 6: Oblivious to Surrender

Our nation has been invaded many times in the past, most notably by the Kai, but we have always prevailed. Citizens of other nations may claim that the war is lost and that the nation is at an end, but not ours.

We know how to keep a cool head, allowing us to maintain the loyalty of the people for longer than would otherwise be possible. A little drink to forget the troubles of the world does not hurt either.

Effect: War exhaustion: -0.03.

Idea 7: Enlightened Sages of Liukhexingzhe

In most lands, being sober is considered to be the most intelligent state of being, with the mind not being clouded with liquor. Here in Liukhexingzhe we know otherwise, and have our most intelligent act accordingly.

The enlightened masters imbue the strongest drinks in order to ascend past petty concerns and create the greatest of innovations. Some of our most revolutionary and effective strategies, devices, and laws have been created in this manner, and there are surely many more to come.

Effect: Idea cost: -10%.

Ambition: Liukhexingzhe Ambition

Effect: Caravan power: +20%.

P'ezarang (Y39) — P'ezarangi Ideas

Traditions: P'ezarangi Traditions

Effect: Global manpower modifier: +15%; Province warscore cost: -15%.

Idea 1: The Dancing Breeze

The Dancing Breeze is the fighting style of P'ezarang, a special technique that utilizes staves, manipulation of the wind to blow enemies away, and for the harpy masters sharp talons are also integrated into this martial art. The Dancing Breeze is a defensive style of fighting, which then allows its users to fight on for longer than regular troops on the battlefield.

Effect: Army morale: +10%.

Idea 2: Teachings of Dasheng

P'ezarang is a nation populated by a mix of devout harpies and humans, a union that was created when the third Martial Master of P'ezarang, Dasheng, converted the harpies to the Transmutative Path. Dasheng himself was a zealous master who sought to spread his fighting style to everyone he came across.

Every person he defeated joined his school, and eventually Dasheng defeated a group of wild harpies who were raiding villages in Thidinkai. He introduced them to the Xianjie, where he spent his final days instilling the aspects of the Transmutative Path to all the followers he gained throughout his journey.

Effect: True faith tolerance: +2.

Idea 3: Midnight Masked Ceremonies

Originally a sacred dance performed for the warriors who died in battle, it soon became a celebrated festival for civilians who gather at their local temple at midnight to partake in singing, mock battles, and dances. Many of the participants in these festivals also wear masks resembling demons, which are said to be used to ward off evil spirits.

Effect: War exhaustion: -0.03.

Idea 4: Shifu of the Mountains

Harpy sifuu, or masters, are known in many old mythical tales as teachers to famous martial heroes who trained in the southern mountains of the Xianjie. This reputation as a wise and mystical group of masters helped integrate the harpies to the legends and culture of the Xianjie, bolstering their image in the neighboring temples.

Effect: Prestige decay: -1%; Army tradition: +0.5.

Idea 5: Custodian of the South

While the Wulin claims to be the head of all the other Xiaken, the truth of the matter is that they hold next to no sway the further a temple is from Xiadao. P'ezarang, being the biggest Xiaken in the south of Xiadao, has used their size as an advantage to negotiate trading benefits from the smaller Xiaken in exchange for offering protection to the border temples against foreign invaders and ambitious masters in the Xianjie.

Effect: Domestic trade power: +10%.

Idea 6: P'ezarang Yanfu

The capital of P'ezarang is a popular destination for their unique style of clothing, called yanfu by the locals, which is an ancient Xianjie style consisting of a robe worn as the upper garment while having a pleated skirt as the lower garment. Many P'ezarangi harpies adorn the yanfu style during their travels outside their territory, which has vastly increased their popularity abroad.

Effect: Diplomatic reputation: +100%; Improve relations: +20%.

Idea 7: The Divine Wind

With guns becoming more commonplace in the wars of Yanshen, the monks of P'ezarang found great success using their martial art to deflect bullets and even weaken the impact of artillery. As a result, many Xianjie harpies were nicknamed the 'Divine Wind' by their enemies.

Effect: Fire damage received: -10%.

Ambition: P'ezarang Ambition

Effect: State maintenance: -25%.
